drafted_by: Claude, 2026-11-13; revised 2026-11-13 on the project owner's corrections
disclosure: Not fully blind to earlier pipeline results. The spec asks for a gold set written before any pipeline output is seen. These annotations were drafted on 2026-11-13, after the M2 and M3 runs, by someone who had seen their output, and revised the same day on the project owner's corrections. Every row is taken from the text of a primary source, not from the database, and each row carries the source and the words it rests on.
level_convention: Levels follow the project's rule (SPEC 3.4): any 'Chief ... Officer' or its abbreviation is c_level, as is a President who is not a Vice President; otherwise a title with 'Vice President' is vp; 'Head of' is head; everything else is other and outside the scope. 'unit' names the subsidiary or business unit when the title is scoped to one.

basecamp.how: The company's own conference page, as fetched by the pipeline and read from its cache.

gtmnow.how: Third party, not a primary source.

approval: The project owner reviewed the rows and their source evidence in chat on 2026-11-13 and approved them. The rows were read from Campfire's own pages listed under 'sources'.
decisions: Titles are kept exactly as the source writes them, and levels follow the project's existing rule.
A person whose title has both 'Vice President' and 'Chief ... Officer' is c_level by that rule and also counts toward VP coverage ('counts_toward').
Company-level and subsidiary- or unit-level roles are kept separate ('scope', 'unit'). A unit-level office is never the company-wide single-holder role.
If recall falls below the target, the actual result is reported. The gold set is not changed to pass.
Chris McDonough is a secondary-source candidate, kept apart from the strict primary-source gold set.
Paul Nichols's current CTO status stays unknown.
